strengths: The core idea of replacing rigid pixel-aligned or voxel-aligned Gaussian primitives with sub-pixel 2D detected keypoints ('Off-the-Grid') combined with an adaptive patch-entropy density allocation is conceptually sound, well-motivated, and novel in feed-forward 3DGS.

The method achieves superior or highly competitive rendering quality (notably on DL3DV) while utilizing significantly fewer primitives (up to 7x fewer primitives than pixels, and less than half of AnySplat's count), demonstrating high representational efficiency.

The self-supervised fine-tuning formulation carefully balances rendering loss with geometric consistency (depth, normals) and teacher regularization, uniquely leading to improved camera pose and intrinsics estimation compared to prior fine-tuning approaches like AnySplat which degraded backbone geometry.
The ablation study is clean and convincingly validates the necessity of sub-pixel detection over dense pixel grids, multi-density adaptation, and the learned multi-view confidence mechanism.
weaknesses: While computational efficiency in terms of primitive count is emphasized, practical runtime metrics (e.g., inference latency per frame, peak memory consumption during feed-forward inference, and rendering FPS) are missing and should be quantitatively documented.

Performance on the synthetic Charge dataset shows mixed quantitative results (notably lower PSNR on sparse views), which the authors attribute to field-of-view cropping and distant background artifacts, but this remains a drawback in sparse unconstrained settings.

The multi-density patch partitioning relies on fixed heuristic thresholds (55% low, 35% medium, 15% high entropy) adopted from prior work, without analysis or exploration into how varying these thresholds impacts the trade-off between visual quality and primitive count.

strengths: Well-motivated concept: Addressing the inefficiency and rigidity of pixel-aligned and voxel-aligned primitive placement in feed-forward 3DGS is an important problem. Formulating primitive placement as sub-pixel keypoint detection via spatial soft-argmax (DSNT) is elegant and well-executed.

Substantial primitive reduction with competitive/superior rendering quality: The proposed Off-The-Grid representation achieves state-of-the-art novel view synthesis results on DL3DV while utilizing far fewer primitives (~7x fewer than pixel-aligned approaches), mitigating line-shaped grid artifacts and excessive memory footprint.

Effective multi-view confidence and end-to-end training framework: Incorporating learned confidence for multi-view fusion, self-rendering guidance, and geometric consistency (depth and normal map constraints) effectively prevents redundant Gaussians and stabilizes pose/depth optimization without relying on external 3D ground truth.

Thorough ablation study and analysis on foundational backbone: Table 3 clearly validates the individual impacts of continuous primitive detection, adaptive density, and learned confidence. Furthermore, Table 2 and the supplementary material demonstrate that fine-tuning with rendering supervision preserves and even enhances camera pose and intrinsics estimation compared to baseline fine-tuning strategies (e.g., AnySplat).
weaknesses: Heuristic nature of adaptive density allocation: The multi-density allocation relies on fixed, pre-defined entropy percentiles (55% low, 35% medium, 15% high) computed via 2D image entropy rather than an end-to-end learned or content-adaptive dynamic budgeting mechanism.

Quantitative trade-offs on the Charge benchmark: In Table 1, on the synthetic Charge dataset with sparse views (3 and 6 views), the method falls behind DepthSplat and FLARE in PSNR. While the authors attribute this to background handling and square cropping differences, further discussion and mitigation of these field-of-view discrepancies would strengthen the evaluation.

Heavy computational and memory requirements: Fine-tuning a 1B-parameter foundation model (VGGT) requires specialized high-memory hardware (140 GB VRAM GPU), which poses a barrier to easy reproducibility and training accessibility.

Missing runtime profiling: While the reduction in Gaussian primitive count is well-documented, the manuscript lacks explicit benchmarks detailing end-to-end feed-forward latency, peak memory consumption during inference, and real-time rendering frame rates (FPS) compared to AnySplat and pixel-aligned baselines.

strengths: Principled and well-motivated formulation: moving away from rigid pixel-aligned or voxel-aligned grids towards continuous, sub-pixel keypoint detection (via DSNT/soft-argmax) addresses a fundamental inefficiency and artifact source in feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Efficient primitive allocation: the combination of entropy-based multi-density patch allocation and multi-view confidence filtering achieves competitive or superior novel view synthesis quality on DL3DV while reducing primitive counts by a factor of 3x to 7x compared to baselines.

Geometric regularization and self-improvement: the proposed training formulation (coupling self-rendering, multi-view depth/normal consistency, and teacher geometry constraints) avoids geometric collapse and demonstrates measurable improvements in camera pose estimation over the underlying VGGT backbone on the Charge benchmark.
Thorough ablation study: Table 3 clearly isolates the contributions of sub-pixel detection versus pixel grids (at multiple resolutions), adaptive density, and multi-view confidence pruning.

Clarity and qualitative evidence: the paper is well-written, with high-quality visual comparisons demonstrating cleaner geometry and reduced floaters/grid artifacts, especially under extrapolated and zoomed-in viewpoints (Figures 6 and 7).
weaknesses: Mixed performance on synthetic benchmark (Charge): while DL3DV shows clear gains, on the Charge dataset under sparse view setups (3 and 6 views), PSNR and SSIM are lower than DepthSplat and FLARE. While the authors explain this by square image cropping and background covisibility issues, it remains an empirical drawback.

Mild degradation in metric depth estimation: Table 2 shows that fine-tuning slightly worsens depth accuracy metrics (AbsRel and delta < 1.25) compared to the raw VGGT model on Charge, indicating that photometric rendering supervision can induce small geometric drift in distant or background regions.

Heuristic patch entropy thresholds: the adaptive density allocation relies on hard-coded percentile cutoffs (55% low, 35% medium, 15% high) determined per-image, which may not dynamically scale well to scenes with entirely uniform or predominantly complex geometry.

Lack of detailed runtime and memory analysis: while the paper mentions reconstructing scenes 'within seconds' and using fewer primitives, it lacks explicit latency and memory profiling across different pipeline stages (VGGT backbone inference, U-Net decoder, unprojection, and rendering) during test-time.

strengths: Well-motivated paradigm shift from rigid pixel-/voxel-aligned 3DGS prediction to continuous sub-pixel primitive detection using differentiable soft-argmax (DSNT).

High primitive efficiency: achieves an 86% reduction in primitive count (~0.14 primitives per pixel compared to 1.0 in pixel-aligned baselines) while simultaneously achieving superior novel view synthesis metrics across six benchmark datasets.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple diverse indoor, outdoor, and synthetic benchmarks (DL3DV, Tanks & Temples, Mip-NeRF 360, 7Scenes, Charge, SCRREAM) demonstrating consistent gains over strong pose-free baselines (AnySplat, DepthAnything3).

Sound ablation studies that isolate the advantages of off-the-grid placement over pixel-aligned and 3D offset approaches, as well as the impact of adaptive density allocation, confidence pruning, and geometry consistency supervision.
weaknesses: The patch density assignment is governed by a handcrafted heuristic (fixed percentiles on grayscale Shannon entropy) rather than a learned end-to-end mechanism or visual feature complexity measure, which may be suboptimal for complex textures or varying resolutions.

The paper lacks explicit measurements of inference runtimes, memory footprint during inference, and rendering frame rates (FPS), reporting only primitive counts (#G/pix) rather than wall-clock efficiency gains.

The evaluation setup relies on a two-pass feed-forward scheme ($N$ views for reconstruction, $N+T$ views for target pose registration) to handle pose-free evaluation, which adds inference overhead and should be explicitly analyzed.

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods, which typically rely on rigid pixel-aligned or voxel-aligned grids that lead to redundant primitives, high memory overhead, and grid artifacts.

The combination of continuous sub-pixel primitive detection via spatial soft-argmax (DSNT), Shannon entropy-guided adaptive primitive allocation, and confidence-based multi-view pruning is technically sensible, elegant, and effective.

Strong quantitative and qualitative results: achieves substantial novel view synthesis improvements over state-of-the-art pose-free baselines (AnySplat, DepthAnything3) across six diverse benchmarks while using approximately 7x fewer primitives (86% reduction).

Comprehensive experimental analysis, including geometry evaluation (depth and camera pose accuracy), and thorough ablation studies isolating the benefits of off-the-grid placement, adaptive density, and confidence-based pruning.
weaknesses: The patch density allocation relies on a handcrafted heuristic (Shannon entropy over 2D grayscale intensity histograms) rather than an end-to-end learned or geometry-aware allocation strategy, which may over-allocate primitives to flat high-frequency textures while under-allocating to low-contrast geometric edges.

Colors are directly assigned via bilinear interpolation of the source image RGBs, eliminating the ability to model view-dependent specular effects or spherical harmonics, which limits performance in non-Lambertian scenes.

While the paper reports significant reductions in primitive counts (#G/pix), it lacks an empirical breakdown of runtime latency and computational overhead (e.g., U-Net feature extraction, bilinear interpolation, and rasterization throughput) compared to pixel-aligned and voxel-aligned baselines.

Minor presentation omissions, such as a missing citation marker on page 6 ('SCRREAM [] 7Scenes [49]') and lack of explicit hyperparameter sensitivity analysis for the entropy threshold percentiles (55%/35%/15%).

strengths: The core idea of 'Off-The-Grid' Gaussians—replacing rigid pixel-aligned or voxel-aligned grids with differentiable sub-pixel primitive detection via convolutional heatmaps and DSNT—is conceptually elegant, well-motivated, and directly tackles the representation redundancy in feed-forward 3DGS.

The approach achieves significant primitive compression, utilizing roughly 7 times fewer primitives than pixel-aligned alternatives (a primitive-to-pixel ratio of ~0.14 vs 1.0) while simultaneously improving rendering fidelity.

Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations across six diverse datasets (DL3DV, Charge, SCRREAM, 7scenes, Tanks and Temples, MipNeRF360) show consistent gains over relevant pose-free feed-forward baselines (AnySplat and DA3-Giant).

The paper includes solid ablation studies (Table 3 and Table 4) that isolate the contribution of sub-pixel primitive placement versus standard pixel-aligned and 3D offset baselines, alongside the effects of the adaptive density scheme and confidence pruning.

Self-supervised fine-tuning of the VGGT backbone with multi-view consistency, camera intrinsics regularization, and teacher losses demonstrates tangible improvements in geometry and intrinsic camera parameters over AnySplat's fine-tuning approach.
weaknesses: The adaptive density strategy relies heavily on an empirical heuristic: grayscale Shannon entropy with fixed quantile thresholds (55%/35%/15% for 16/32/64 primitives). It lacks exploration into learning-based density allocation or incorporating geometric/semantic variance.

The paper does not report concrete runtime and latency metrics (e.g., feed-forward inference time per frame/scene, memory consumption during inference, rendering FPS) compared to AnySplat and standard 3DGS, despite efficiency being a primary selling point.

Comparisons with other existing pose-free feed-forward methods (e.g., NoPoSplat, Splatt3R, PF3Splat) or generalizable 3DGS methods evaluated under known poses to isolate the exact rendering capacity of the decoder are limited.

The model assigns view-independent interpolated RGB colors directly to primitives without modeling view-dependent effects (e.g., spherical harmonics), which limits rendering quality on non-Lambertian surfaces and scenes with complex lighting.
